newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tristate says privatisation plan lapsed.
newsitem.headline: Tristate says privatisation plan lapsed.

text.p: Garment and property concern Tristate Holdings Ltd said on Monday its privatisation plan lapsed after it failed to obtain majority approval from minority shareholders in a general meeting last Friday.

Tristate said minority shareholders holding 14.79 million shares -- representing 83.3 percent of the 17.75 million minority-held shares voted at the meeting -- backed the privatisation proposal, below the required 90 percent.
Tristate said the scheme would lapse and no application would be made to the stock exchange to withdraw the listing of the company shares.
"The directors confirm that they have no intention of making any material changes to the business of the company or any significant redeployment of its fixed assets," it said.
Tristate's controlling shareholders hold 83.22 million shares or 67.2 percent of the company.
Trading in the company shares resumed on Monday after a one-day suspension on Friday and were down HK$0.45 at HK$4.15 in late morming trade.
In January, Tristate's controlling shareholders proposed a privatisation plan under which minority shareholders would receive HK$4.80 in cash for each Tristate share held.
